subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Edge Case Problem
description: A 60-second lesson on The Edge Case Problem.

hook.text: Self-driving cars handle 99% of driving perfectly. The last 1% is where people get hurt.

buildup.text: Edge cases are rare situations: a mattress falling off a truck, a child chasing a ball, unusual road markings.

discovery.text: Humans handle edge cases through intuition. Machines must be programmed for scenarios they've never seen.

twist.text: There are effectively infinite edge cases. Every rare event creates another scenario to solve.

climax.text: The long tail of edge cases is why full autonomy is years away despite billions in investment.

punchline.text: The last 1% of driving is where 99% of the difficulty lives.

quiz.question: What are edge cases in autonomous driving?
options: Rare, unusual situations that the system wasn't specifically trained for
